passages.text: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
The choirmaster led music in worship.
This psalm is a song for worship.

passages.text: O God of my praise, be not silent.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm for the choirmaster.
David speaks to God.
God is the God whom David praises.
David asks God to not remain silent.
passages.original: לַ֭מְנַצֵּחַ לְדָוִ֣ד מִזְמ֑וֹר אֱלֹהֵ֥י תְ֝הִלָּתִ֗י אַֽל־ תֶּחֱרַֽשׁ׃

passages.text: For wicked and deceitful mouths open against me; they speak against me with lying tongues.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David speaks to God.
Wicked people open their mouths against David.
Deceitful people speak against David.
They use lying tongues.
They speak lies about David.
passages.original: כִּ֤י פִ֪י רָשָׁ֡ע וּֽפִי־ מִ֭רְמָה עָלַ֣י פָּתָ֑חוּ דִּבְּר֥וּ אִ֝תִּ֗י לְשׁ֣וֹן שָֽׁקֶר׃

passages.text: They surround me with hateful words and attack me without cause.
passages.sermon:
David speaks in this psalm.
David is surrounded by people who hate him.
These people use hateful words against David.
They attack David.
They have no reason to attack him.
passages.original: וְדִבְרֵ֣י שִׂנְאָ֣ה סְבָב֑וּנִי וַיִּֽלָּחֲמ֥וּנִי חִנָּֽם׃

passages.text: In return for my love they accuse me, but I am a man of prayer.
passages.sermon:
The enemies accuse me.
I show them love.
They return my love with hatred.
I pray to God.
I am a man of prayer.
passages.original: תַּֽחַת־ אַהֲבָתִ֥י יִשְׂטְנ֗וּנִי וַאֲנִ֥י תְפִלָּֽה׃

passages.text: They repay me evil for good, and hatred for my love.
passages.sermon: The enemies act against me.\r\nThey give me evil when I do good.\r\nThey show me hatred when I show them love.
passages.original: וַיָּ֘שִׂ֤ימוּ עָלַ֣י רָ֭עָה תַּ֣חַת טוֹבָ֑ה וְ֝שִׂנְאָ֗ה תַּ֣חַת אַהֲבָתִֽי׃

passages.text: Set over him a wicked man; let an accuser stand at his right hand.
passages.sermon:
The psalmist speaks about his enemies.
He asks God to appoint a wicked man over his enemy.
He asks God to place an accuser at his enemy’s right hand.
The wicked man will have authority over the enemy.
The accuser will stand beside the enemy to oppose him.
passages.original: הַפְקֵ֣ד עָלָ֣יו רָשָׁ֑ע וְ֝שָׂטָ֗ן יַעֲמֹ֥ד עַל־ יְמִינֽוֹ׃

passages.text: When he is tried, let him be found guilty, and may his prayer be regarded as sin.
passages.sermon:
This verse speaks about a wicked man.
He faces judgment.
The judge examines him.
The judge finds him guilty.
God does not accept his prayer.
God counts his prayer as sin.
passages.original: בְּ֭הִשָּׁ֣פְטוֹ יֵצֵ֣א רָשָׁ֑ע וּ֝תְפִלָּת֗וֹ תִּהְיֶ֥ה לַֽחֲטָאָֽה׃

passages.text: May his days be few; may another take his position.
passages.sermon: The psalmist speaks about a wicked man.\r\nHe asks God to make this man's life short.\r\nHe asks God to let another person take the wicked man's place.
passages.original: יִֽהְיֽוּ־ יָמָ֥יו מְעַטִּ֑ים פְּ֝קֻדָּת֗וֹ יִקַּ֥ח אַחֵֽר׃

passages.text: May his children be fatherless and his wife a widow.
passages.sermon:
This passage speaks about a wicked man.
\r\nThe wicked man will face judgment.
\r\nHis children will become orphans.
\r\nHis wife will become a widow.
passages.original: יִֽהְיוּ־ בָנָ֥יו יְתוֹמִ֑ים וְ֝אִשְׁתּוֹ אַלְמָנָֽה׃

passages.text: May his children wander as beggars, seeking sustenance far from their ruined homes.
passages.sermon:
His children will wander.
His children will become beggars.
They will search for food.
They will look for help far from their destroyed homes.
passages.original: וְנ֤וֹעַ יָנ֣וּעוּ בָנָ֣יו וְשִׁאֵ֑לוּ וְ֝דָרְשׁ֗וּ מֵחָרְבוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: May the creditor seize all he owns, and strangers plunder the fruits of his labor.
passages.sermon: A creditor takes everything he owns.\r\nStrangers take the results of his hard work.\r\n
passages.original: יְנַקֵּ֣שׁ נ֭וֹשֶׁה לְכָל־ אֲשֶׁר־ ל֑וֹ וְיָבֹ֖זּוּ זָרִ֣ים יְגִיעֽוֹ׃

passages.text: May there be no one to extend kindness to him, and no one to favor his fatherless children.
passages.sermon:
This verse speaks about a man who faces judgment from God.
No one shows him kindness.
No one helps his children.
His children are orphans.
No one gives favor to his orphans.
passages.original: אַל־ יְהִי־ ל֭וֹ מֹשֵׁ֣ךְ חָ֑סֶד וְֽאַל־ יְהִ֥י ח֝וֹנֵ֗ן לִיתוֹמָֽיו׃

passages.text: May his descendants be cut off; may their name be blotted out from the next generation.
passages.sermon:
This passage speaks about a wicked man.
The wicked man has descendants.
May all his descendants be cut off.
May his family line end.
May people erase his name from the next generation.
May no one remember him in the future.
passages.original: יְהִֽי־ אַחֲרִית֥וֹ לְהַכְרִ֑ית בְּד֥וֹר אַ֝חֵ֗ר יִמַּ֥ח שְׁמָֽם׃

passages.text: May the iniquity of his fathers be remembered before the LORD, and the sin of his mother never be blotted out.
passages.sermon:
God is the Lord.
God remembers the sins of his fathers.
God does not erase the sin of his mother.
God keeps these sins before Him.
passages.original: יִזָּכֵ֤ר׀ עֲוֺ֣ן אֲ֭בֹתָיו אֶל־ יְהוָ֑ה וְחַטַּ֥את אִ֝מּ֗וֹ אַל־ תִּמָּֽח׃

passages.text: May their sins always remain before the LORD, that He may cut off their memory from the earth.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is God.
Their sins stand before the Lord at all times.
The Lord does not forget their sins.
The Lord removes their memory from the earth.
passages.original: יִהְי֣וּ נֶֽגֶד־ יְהוָ֣ה תָּמִ֑יד וְיַכְרֵ֖ת מֵאֶ֣רֶץ זִכְרָֽם׃

passages.text: For he never thought to show kindness, but pursued the poor and needy and brokenhearted, even to their death.
passages.sermon:
This man did not remember to show kindness.
He did not act with mercy.
He chased after the poor.
He hunted the needy.
He pursued those with broken hearts.
He followed them even to their death.
passages.original: יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר׀ לֹ֥א זָכַר֮ עֲשׂ֪וֹת חָ֥סֶד וַיִּרְדֹּ֡ף אִישׁ־ עָנִ֣י וְ֭אֶבְיוֹן וְנִכְאֵ֨ה לֵבָ֬ב לְמוֹתֵֽת׃

passages.text: The cursing that he loved, may it fall on him; the blessing in which he refused to delight, may it be far from him.
passages.sermon:
He loved to curse.
The curse came upon him.
He did not want blessing.
The blessing stayed far from him.
passages.original: וַיֶּאֱהַ֣ב קְ֭לָלָה וַתְּבוֹאֵ֑הוּ וְֽלֹא־ חָפֵ֥ץ בִּ֝בְרָכָ֗ה וַתִּרְחַ֥ק מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: The cursing that he wore like a coat, may it soak into his body like water, and into his bones like oil.
passages.sermon:
This man loved to curse others.
He wore cursing like a coat.
The curse entered his body like water.
The curse went into his bones like oil.
passages.original: וַיִּלְבַּ֥שׁ קְלָלָ֗ה כְּמַ֫דּ֥וֹ וַתָּבֹ֣א כַמַּ֣יִם בְּקִרְבּ֑וֹ וְ֝כַשֶּׁ֗מֶן בְּעַצְמוֹתָֽיו׃

passages.text: May it be like a robe wrapped about him, like a belt tied forever around him.
passages.sermon:
The curse covers him like a robe.
He wraps the curse around himself.
The curse stays with him like a belt.
He ties the curse around himself forever.
passages.original: תְּהִי־ ל֭וֹ כְּבֶ֣גֶד יַעְטֶ֑ה וּ֝לְמֵ֗זַח תָּמִ֥יד יַחְגְּרֶֽהָ׃

passages.text: May this be the LORD’s reward to my accusers, to those who speak evil against me.
passages.sermon: The LORD gives a reward to my accusers.\r\nMy accusers speak evil against me.\r\nThis is the reward from the LORD for them.
passages.original: זֹ֤את פְּעֻלַּ֣ת שֹׂ֭טְנַי מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וְהַדֹּבְרִ֥ים רָ֝֗ע עַל־ נַפְשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: But You, O GOD, the Lord, deal kindly with me for the sake of Your name; deliver me by the goodness of Your loving devotion.
passages.sermon:
God is the Lord.
God has power and authority.
God, act kindly toward me.
Do this because of Your name.
Your name is holy and great.
Your loving devotion is good.
Save me by Your goodness.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֤ה׀ יְה֘וִ֤ה אֲדֹנָ֗י עֲ‍ֽשֵׂה־ אִ֭תִּי לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמֶ֑ךָ כִּי־ ט֥וֹב חַ֝סְדְּךָ֗ הַצִּילֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: For I am poor and needy; my heart is wounded within me.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is David.
David is poor.
David is needy.
David’s heart is wounded inside him.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ עָנִ֣י וְאֶבְי֣וֹן אָנֹ֑כִי וְ֝לִבִּ֗י חָלַ֥ל בְּקִרְבִּֽי׃

passages.text: I am fading away like a lengthening shadow; I am shaken off like a locust.
passages.sermon:
I am weak and helpless.
I am fading away.
I am like a shadow that grows longer and disappears.
People push me aside.
I am like a locust that is shaken off and cast away.
passages.original: כְּצֵל־ כִּנְטוֹת֥וֹ נֶהֱלָ֑כְתִּי נִ֝נְעַ֗רְתִּי כָּֽאַרְבֶּֽה׃

passages.text: My knees are weak from fasting, and my body grows lean and gaunt.
passages.sermon:
I am poor and needy.
My knees are weak because I have fasted.
My body has become thin.
I have lost my strength and fat.
passages.original: בִּ֭רְכַּי כָּשְׁל֣וּ מִצּ֑וֹם וּ֝בְשָׂרִ֗י כָּחַ֥שׁ מִשָּֽׁמֶן׃

passages.text: I am an object of scorn to my accusers; when they see me, they shake their heads.
passages.sermon: My accusers scorn me.\r\nThey see me.\r\nThey shake their heads at me.
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֤י׀ הָיִ֣יתִי חֶרְפָּ֣ה לָהֶ֑ם יִ֝רְא֗וּנִי יְנִיע֥וּן רֹאשָֽׁם׃

passages.text: Help me, O LORD my God; save me according to Your loving devotion.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is weak and suffering.
The speaker prays to God.
The speaker calls God “LORD” and “my God.”
The speaker asks God for help.
The speaker asks God to save him.
The speaker trusts in God’s loving devotion.
The speaker asks God to save him because of God’s loving devotion.
passages.original: עָ֭זְרֵנִי יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑י ה֭וֹשִׁיעֵ֣נִי כְחַסְדֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: Let them know that this is Your hand, that You, O LORD, have done it.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God acts with power.
God does this work.
Let them see Your action, LORD.
Let them know Your hand did this.
passages.original: וְֽ֭יֵדְעוּ כִּי־ יָ֣דְךָ זֹּ֑את אַתָּ֖ה יְהוָ֣ה עֲשִׂיתָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Though they curse, You will bless. When they rise up, they will be put to shame, but Your servant will rejoice.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
\r\nSome people curse.
\r\nYou, LORD, bless.
\r\nThey rise up.
\r\nThey feel shame.
\r\nYour servant rejoices.
passages.original: יְקַֽלְלוּ־ הֵמָּה֮ וְאַתָּ֪ה תְבָ֫רֵ֥ךְ קָ֤מוּ׀ וַיֵּבֹ֗שׁוּ וְֽעַבְדְּךָ֥ יִשְׂמָֽח׃

passages.text: May my accusers be clothed with disgrace; may they wear their shame like a robe.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David had enemies who accused him.
David asked God to act.
David said, “Let my accusers wear disgrace.”
David said, “Let them cover themselves with shame like a robe.”
passages.original: יִלְבְּשׁ֣וּ שׂוֹטְנַ֣י כְּלִמָּ֑ה וְיַעֲט֖וּ כַמְעִ֣יל בָּשְׁתָּֽם׃

passages.text: With my mouth I will thank the LORD profusely; I will praise Him in the presence of many.
passages.sermon:
David speaks this psalm.
David thanks the LORD with his mouth.
David thanks the LORD very much.
David praises the LORD among many people.
David praises the LORD where many can hear.
passages.original: א֘וֹדֶ֤ה יְהוָ֣ה מְאֹ֣ד בְּפִ֑י וּבְת֖וֹךְ רַבִּ֣ים אֲהַֽלְלֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: For He stands at the right hand of the needy one, to save him from the condemners of his soul.
passages.sermon:
God stands beside the needy person.
God stands at the right hand of the needy.
God does this to help the needy person.
God saves the needy person from those who judge his soul.
God protects the needy from those who condemn him.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יַ֭עֲמֹד לִימִ֣ין אֶבְי֑וֹן לְ֝הוֹשִׁ֗יעַ מִשֹּׁפְטֵ֥י נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
